source.stem: Which cell helps to move dust particles out of an organism?

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Viruses can multiply outside living cells.

intelligence.enrichment: Microorganisms can be categorised into groups such as protozoa, fungi, bacteria, and some algae. Viruses are microscopic and acellular, and they multiply when they enter a living cell. Observed or stated features -> microbe category or virus boundary -> correct classification. The learner correctly applies this rule: Microorganisms can be categorised into groups such as protozoa, fungi, bacteria, and some algae. Viruses are microscopic and acellular, and they multiply when they enter a living cell. Anything microscopic is basically a bacterium, so the exact category does not matter.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Microorganisms: friend and foe. The student must decide: Decide how to classify examples such as Amoeba, bread mould, bacteria, some algae, and viruses without treating all microscopic things as the same kind of organism. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Retarget the source onto this Science decision. Keep the source item type. Recalculate the key.
